alt: The FAA air traffic control tower at Philadelphia International Airport rising above the terminal buildings — identical in design to the towers whose copper-wire telecom backbone was being upgraded when a router collapse triggered a nationwide ground stop on November 13, 2026
story: On November 13, 2026, defense contractor L3Harris triggered the second-ever nationwide US aviation ground stop since 9/11 while replacing the FAA's copper-wire telecom backbone with fiber; a router being swapped out flooded the air traffic control network with over 1,000 connection attempts per second, collapsing the system. About 25,000 flights were delayed and 9,000+ cancelled. Transportation Secretary Duffy said the FAA 'is using old equipment.' The first nationwide ground stop since 9/11 — in 2023 — was also caused by contractor error at an FAA system. A 2023 safety review had already warned the network relied on 'obsolete telecommunications technology.'
why_funny: The agency responsible for keeping every US flight safe was already warned in writing that its telecom system was dangerously obsolete — then grounded the entire country during a routine upgrade of the very system it already knew was fragile.
